recommendation_summary: Do now: replace the desk cable with a new Cat6 patch cable routed loosely through the grommet, and plug it into a different router port. Later, only if drops continue: look at the computer's Ethernet link state during a drop, then check the network adapter. Hold the UniFi/switch/Grafana budget. No optional extras are recommended now.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You want dependable calls at the one desk; "future-proof like my group" came from the group's trend, not from an observed failure.
labels.Deleted: UniFi gateway, managed switches, and Grafana dashboard, because two other devices on the same router stay connected during drops, so the router and internet line are not what's failing.
labels.Bottleneck: The desk's own link: a years-old cable squeezed through a tight grommet, or the port or network adapter at either end.
labels.Checked myself: Nothing live; this rests only on what you told me (desk on Ethernet, other devices stay up, old cable in tight grommet, no cable swap tried yet).

note: The reply makes a bounded cable-and-port swap with a conditional next step, removes the network stack by name, and claims no tests it didn't run.
